title: Prompt injection arrives in tool results
why: Wednesday is education. The last three days were a feature video (ledger), a how-it-works diagram (agents calling agents) and a release; none taught threat modelling. Indirect prompt injection (OWASP LLM01) is the risk agent builders underestimate most, and our own docs are unusually honest about it: detection is a second line, narrow tools and approvals are the first.

cards.statement: The injection isn't in the prompt. It's in the *tool result*.
cards.alt: Text card: The injection isn't in the prompt. It's in the tool result. OWASP LLM01, the indirect kind.

cards.headline: Narrow it. *Inspect* it. Hold writes.
cards.sub: Allowlists decide which tools exist for the agent. Inspect gates read results before it does. Writes wait for a person.

carousel.headline: Prompt injection arrives in the *tool result*
carousel.sub: A threat model for agents that read things

carousel.statement: Your agent reads a GitHub issue, a web page, a support ticket. Whoever wrote it *wrote to your agent*.

carousel.eyebrow: 2 / Why the prompt filter misses it
carousel.statement: Checking what the user typed is half the job. The instructions show up *after* the tool call, in the result the agent trusts.
Patterns catch "ignore previous instructions". A paraphrase, another language or encoded text *gets past them*.
The real question: once an agent is convinced, *what can it reach?*

carousel.headline: Narrow, inspect, *hold the writes*
bullets: Per-key tool allowlists: unlisted tools aren't shown
Inspect tool results before the agent reads them
Writes and deletes wait for a person

carousel.headline: Check *every* tool result
carousel.code:
- name: Check tool results for injection
  match: { tools: ["*"] }
  effect: inspect
  config:
    detectors: [injection]
    model_check: { model: gpt-4.1-mini, on_error: allow }
    action: block
    direction: output
carousel.sub: Pattern checks are free; the model check catches paraphrases for one call.

linkedin.text:
Your prompt filter checks what the user typed. The attack arrives in what the agent read.

That's indirect prompt injection (OWASP LLM01), and agents that call tools are built for it. The agent fetches a web page, opens a GitHub issue, pulls a support ticket. Whoever wrote that text is now writing to your agent, inside a tool result it treats as data.

Three things we learned building defences for it into Control Tower:

1. Inspect results, not just requests. Our inspect gates run on tool results and MCP resources before the agent reads them, and mask or block.

2. Don't trust detection alone. Pattern checks catch "ignore previous instructions". A paraphrase, another language or encoded text gets past them. Asking a model catches more, at the cost of a call. Either way it's a second line.

3. Design for the agent that's already convinced. Give each agent its own key with only the tools it needs (the rest aren't even listed to it), and hold writes and deletes for a person to approve.

The carousel has the threat model and the policy.

Control Tower is an open-source, self-hosted gateway for agents, models and MCP tools. Our OWASP LLM Top 10 mapping, limits included, is in the docs. A ⭐ helps others find it: https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

posts:
Your prompt filter checks what the user typed.

The injection arrives in what the agent read: the web page, the GitHub issue, the support ticket. Inside a tool result it treats as data.

A short threat model 🧵
Detection helps, but it's a second line. Patterns catch "ignore previous instructions". Paraphrases, other languages and encoded text get past them. A model check catches more, at the cost of a call.

So design for the agent that's already convinced:

• only the tools it needs (the rest aren't even listed)
• inspect tool results before it reads them
• writes and deletes wait for a human

Control Tower does all three as an open-source, self-hosted gateway for agents and MCP. Our OWASP LLM Top 10 mapping, limits included, is in the repo:
https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower
